UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT, DISTRICT OF WESTBROOK
Ellis v. City of Marion Heights et al., 24-CV-04412

DEFENDANTS' ANSWER

Defendants City of Marion Heights, R. Dowling, and P. Esquivel answer as follows:

1. Admitted that Plaintiff was contacted by Officers Dowling and Esquivel on June 7, 2024.
2. Denied that the contact was without legal basis. Officers were responding to community complaints of suspicious activity.
3. Denied that any force used was excessive. Force used was the minimum necessary to ensure officer safety after Plaintiff became uncooperative.
4. Without sufficient information to admit or deny Plaintiff's medical injuries; same are placed in dispute.
5. Denied any pattern, policy, or custom of excessive force by the City.
6. The individual Defendants assert qualified immunity.

AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES:
A. Qualified immunity (Pearson v. Callahan, 555 U.S. 223).
B. Plaintiff's own conduct contributed to any alleged harm.
C. Failure to mitigate damages.

Dated: August 15, 2024
                                /s/ T. Kowalski
                                City Attorney's Office
